name: Census Bureau Building Permits Survey (BPS)
proposed_use: National generalization of the 'development' growth-score pillar currently fed by NYC DOB-specific data in app/sources/development.py (HousingDatabase, Rezonings — both scoped to NYC's own permit/filing systems). New-unit permit counts by county/place would give any US metro a supply-pipeline signal for the Growth Score without depending on a city having its own open-data portal for development filings.
coverage: national — every US county and permit-issuing place
granularity: county and permit-issuing place (sub-county); also state and CBSA roll-ups
history_start: detailed county/place files 2019-present on the current site; state/MSA text files back to 1995
license: US government work, public domain. No ToS restriction on commercial/product use.
cost: Free. Direct CSV/Excel downloads need no key; the Census Bureau's general API (for programmatic pulls) needs a free key, same pattern as census_api_key already used by CensusAcs.
api_key_notes: Bulk CSV downloads (census.gov/construction/bps) need no key at all. A key is only needed if pulling through the generic data.census.gov API instead of the BPS site's own flat files — this repo's census_api_key would cover that path too if preferred.
rate_limit: None published for the flat-file downloads.
recommendation: Recommend, with a scoping caveat. Genuinely free, national, no new credential type, and it fills a real gap: right now 'development momentum' only exists for NYC because HousingDatabase/Rezonings are built against NYC-specific DOB/DCP open-data endpoints. BPS permit counts are a weaker, coarser proxy for the same idea (raw new-unit permits vs. NYC's richer filing-status/rezoning detail) but they're the only version of this signal available everywhere. Implement this as the generic/national fallback development signal, not a replacement for the NYC-specific sources, which should stay as the higher-fidelity path when available.
